With brother Joe qualifying in the 1951 race Percy Wilson took his turn to become No. 246 in 21:53:55. Like Joe you cannot keep him away from the sporting scene, he recently had a spell in hospital due to a stroke but is now fighting his way back to fitness.

We are saddened to hear that the Percy half of the stalwart Wilson brothers is seriously ill in Bolingbroke Hospital. Percy and Joe featured in our walking teams for many many years and I know that Joe will do all he can to keep the partnership going by conveying to Percy our best wishes for his recovery.

Percy Wilson lost a long and brave fight against illness and died in July. He will be remembered, alongside brother Joe, for his many appearances at walking fixtures, his regular manning of sponging stations on the Brighton Road and particularly for his work with youngsters.
My mind is filled with many thoughts in an endeavour to do justice to the memory of Percy Wilson who died in his 61st year after a long and distressing illness.
